nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § group#0

content.label: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14
content.takeaway: Outage review: Alerting, status page, and config review improved; auto-rollback and Friday freeze open.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#0

content.markdown: Attendees: Dana (facilitator), Marcus (on-call SRE), Leila (payments backend lead), Tomás (release engineering), Kenji (customer support lead)

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#1

content.markdown: This is a blameless review for the checkout outage on Friday, March 14.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § timeline
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#2

content.markdown: At 16:40, a configuration change was deployed to the payments service. This change incorrectly set the gateway connection pool from 50 to 5 connections, instead of the intended 55. This typo caused checkout requests to queue and time out.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § cause#0

content.markdown:
The error-rate alert for checkout fired at 17:02, 22 minutes after the config change. The alert is configured to fire when the checkout error rate exceeds 10% for 15 minutes. Errors surpassed 10% around 16:47, so the alert functioned as designed.

**From the source:** 02

**From the source:** 02

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#3

content.markdown: The incorrect configuration was rolled back at 17:15. Checkout functionality was fully restored by 17:27.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#4

content.markdown: Customers experienced errors for a total of 47 minutes. Approximately 2,300 checkout failures were recorded. Customer support received 140 tickets before the status page was updated.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § alerting_threshold
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § problem#0

content.markdown: The current alert threshold (10% error rate for 15 minutes) is considered too slow for checkout, leading to significant lost revenue.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § solution#0

content.markdown:
A new proposal suggests lowering the checkout error-rate alert to 5% over 5 minutes. This change would have resulted in two noisy pages in the last 30 days, both during payment provider maintenance, which is deemed acceptable.

**From the source:** twice

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § action_item#0

items.text: Lower the checkout error-rate alert to 5% over 5 minutes. Owner: Marcus. Due: Wednesday, March 19.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § status_page_updates
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § problem#1

content.markdown: The status page was updated at 17:20, 40 minutes after errors began. Customers were already discussing the issue on social media before an official update was posted.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § cause#1

content.markdown: Currently, the incident commander is responsible for posting status page updates, but this can be overlooked during critical incident response, as Marcus was busy with the rollback.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § solution#1

content.markdown: Support should be allowed to post status page updates directly, without waiting for the incident commander.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § action_item#1

content.markdown: Support will be empowered to post status-page updates directly.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § config_change_process
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § problem#2

content.markdown:
Configuration changes, unlike code changes, do not undergo code review. They are edited and applied directly via the deploy dashboard, making them susceptible to errors like typos.

**From the source:** two

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § solution#2

content.markdown: The proposal is to subject payments configuration changes to the same review process as code changes.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § config_change_approval

content.markdown:
Config changes to the payments service will require a pull-request review with one approval from the payments team.

**From the source:** payments-team

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § action_item_leila

items.text: Move config into the repo and add approval rule by Friday, March 21.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § proposal_friday_freeze

content.markdown:
Tomás proposes stopping deployments to payments after 15:00 on Fridays, citing that the incident occurred at 16:40 on a Friday when fewer team members were available, potentially slowing recovery.

**From the source:** 00

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § leila_disagreement

content.markdown: Leila disagrees with a Friday deployment freeze, arguing it shifts risk to Monday morning when traffic is higher. She believes the issue was lack of review, not the day, and that recovery time for this incident (25 minutes) was not impacted by it being a Friday.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § tomas_rebuttal

content.markdown: Tomás suggests that while review fixes one cause, fewer people around on Fridays means slower recovery for any cause, and believes a pattern would emerge if more incidents were examined.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § action_item_tomas

items.text: Tomás to pull incidents from the last six months to see if late-Friday deploys are over-represented, and bring findings to the next review on April 2.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § proposal_auto_rollback

content.markdown: Marcus proposes automatic rollback: if the checkout error rate doubles within 10 minutes of a deploy, the pipeline rolls back automatically.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § leila_concerns_rollback

content.markdown: Leila is nervous about automatic rollback for code, especially if a release includes a database migration, as rolling back code without the migration could worsen the situation. Marcus suggests excluding releases with migrations.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § rollback_open_question

content.markdown: Leila wants to know the frequency of database migrations before agreeing to automatic rollback. Dana notes that auto-rollback remains an open question due to unknown migration frequency.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § customer_retries_question

content.markdown: Kenji asks if any of the 2,300 failed checkouts were successfully retried, as this would influence the customer email. Marcus states that payment logs would show this, but no one has checked yet.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § action_item_kenji

items.text: Kenji to draft the customer email.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 2 § timeline_recap

content.markdown:
Timeline recap: change deployed at 16:40, alert at 17:02, rollback at 17:15, recovered at 17:27.

**From the source:** 02

nodes.title: Decisions Made
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#0

content.markdown:
- **Alerting Threshold:** Checkout error-rate alert lowered to 5% over 5 minutes. Marcus to implement by March 19.
- **Status Page Updates:** Support can directly post status page updates. No specific owner or deadline mentioned.
- **Config Change Process:** Payments service config changes require pull-request review with one payments-team approval. Leila to set up by March 21.

nodes.title: Open Questions/Actions for Next Review (April 2)
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#1

content.markdown:
- **Friday Deployment Freeze:** Tomás to analyze incidents from the last six months for late-Friday deploy over-representation.
- **Automatic Rollback:** Open question due to concerns about database migrations. Leila wants to know migration frequency.
- **Failed Checkout Retries:** Kenji to draft customer email; Marcus to investigate if failed checkouts were successfully retried.

nodes.title: Key Findings
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#2

content.markdown:
- The config change reduced the gateway connection pool from 50 to 5 (intended 55), causing checkout requests to queue and time out.
- The alert fired 22 minutes after the config change because the threshold was 10% errors over 15 minutes.
- The status page update was delayed by 40 minutes, as the incident commander (Marcus) was focused on rollback.
- Config changes currently bypass code review, allowing typos to go unnoticed.
